messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [INCIDENT] 2233330000 - High rate of 429s observed for tenant "aurigafin" in dedicated pool eu-west-2-ded-42. Paging SRE on-call. Severity: P1. Affected: production scoring endpoints. Spike started ~2026-03-15T10:12:00Z. Current 429 rate: ~37% over last 5m. Monitor: https://redwood.monitor/incident/2233330000

Marta Rivera: I'm on it. @Kevin Lowe can you confirm whether the dedicated pool is at capacity or if tenant throttling triggered?

Kevin Lowe: checking... pulling metrics and logs now. Seen a sudden batch start from aurigafin origin at 10:10 UTC. Pool GPU util spiked to ~84%, queue length spiked, per-tenant token counters show aurigafin saturating its burst window. Sample 429 headers captured.

Kevin Lowe: ```json
{ "ts":"2026-03-15T10:12:23Z", "tenant":"aurigafin", "status":429, "reason":"rate_limit", "x-rate-limit-remaining":0, "pool":"eu-west-2-ded-42" }
{ "ts":"2026-03-15T10:12:24Z", "tenant":"aurigafin", "status":429, "reason":"burst_exceeded", "x-rate-limit-reset":"2026-03-15T10:13:00Z" }
```

Lee Chen: runtime note — looks like a large EOD scoring job (long sequences + cold KV load). Two-pronged mitigation: 1) emergency tenant override (temporary lift of per-second/burst limits), 2) route non-sensitive/public endpoints to hosted fallback (reduce dedicated pool load). I can add a routing rule for public paths to hosted.v2-lowcost.

Jamal Ortiz: From account — aurigafin is doing an end-of-day batch. Contract committed baseline is 12k qps with monthly bursts defined; emergency clause allows temporary bump subject to SRE + ops. I approve a short emergency lift to 60k burst for up to 30m if SRE/ops confirm.

Sophia Patel: Customer success on the line. Auriga says they can stagger if we give a short lift. @Auriga Ops (customer) can you confirm you can throttle if we increase capacity?

Auriga Ops (customer): We can stagger internally if you lift. Prefer a 20m lift to finish current window.

Marta Rivera: OK action plan: Kevin apply tenant override now; Lee add fallback routing for non-critical endpoints; I'll monitor metrics and request IDs. Steps: 1) set override, 2) push routing rule, 3) monitor error rate & latency, 4) revoke override when stable.

Kevin Lowe: running command now:
```bash
redwoodctl tenants override-set aurigafin --burst=60000 --duration=20m --reason='emergency-lift-2233330000'
```
Response: OK queued, policy applied to pool eu-west-2-ded-42. Effective in ~5s.

Kevin Lowe: Confirmation: override active. Observed 429 rate dropping: 37% -> 4% in first 90s, now ~0.8% over last 2m. GPU queue length returning to normal.

Lee Chen: pushed routing rule for non-critical public paths:
```yaml
- match: tenant==aurigafin && path =~ '/public/*'
  route: hosted.v2-lowcost
  ttl: 30m
```
Non-critical endpoints now routed away from dedicated pool.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation applied. Current summary: errors ~0.8%, avg latency +35ms vs baseline, pool utilization ~62%. Incident remains open for observation. Pager auto-rearm in 30m.

Jamal Ortiz: I've notified legal and CS of the emergency lift per contract clause. I've logged the override for billing/credit check.

Sophia Patel: I'll coordinate with the customer to confirm they finish the backlog and then throttle. Please send me request IDs for verification.

Marta Rivera: Post-mitigation next steps: 1) open postmortem ticket INC-2233330000, 2) collect request IDs & prompt sets, 3) recommend job-scheduling constraints for customer to avoid bursts (we'll propose a rate-limiter on their scheduler), 4) review contract burst terms. Handoff to Kevin for 2-hour watch.

Kevin Lowe: Handoff accepted. I'll monitor dashboard and alert if error rate rises >2% or GPU util >80%. Will revoke override after 20m or earlier if customer finishes.

Auriga Ops (customer): Thanks — current window finishing in ~12 minutes, we'll throttle then. Appreciate the quick response.

incident-bot: Status update: mitigated -> monitoring. Timeline logged. Will auto-close if stable for 1h.

Marta Rivera: Please add any additional notes to ticket INC-2233330000 and assign follow-up actions: Lee (routing + fallback test), Product (quota policy review), CS (customer job guidance). Closing active coordination, leaving incident in monitoring state.
